extracted.intended_audience: Early-career researchers at U.S. academic institutions, DOE National Laboratories, and Office of Science User Facilities interested in DOE Office of Science Early Career Research Program awards
extracted.subtask_description: Applying for the Department of Energy Office of Science Early Career Research Program (five-year awards) by submitting a mandatory pre-application and, if encouraged, a full application for research aligned to one of the Office of Science program offices and their programmatic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — position and employer
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the program, a researcher must be an untenured, tenure-track assistant or associate professor at a U.S. academic institution or a full-time employee at a DOE National Laboratory or Office of Science User Facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is limited to those specific appointment types and employer categories (U.S. academic institutions, DOE National Laboratories, Office of Science User Facilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — time since doctorate
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible researchers must be within 10 years of having earned a doctorate degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 10-year post-PhD window is an explicit cutoff for eligibility; applicants should ensure their doctorate date falls within this period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and award duration (institution type differentiated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards to an institution of higher education will be approximately $875,000 over five years and awards to a DOE National Laboratory or Office of Science User Facility will be approximately $2,750,000 over five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All awards are five-year projects, but the approximate total funding differs substantially based on whether the award goes to a university or to a DOE lab/user facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic topical fit — eligible program offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Early career researchers may apply to one of seven Office of Science program offices: Advanced Scientific Computing Research; Biological and Environmental Research; Basic Energy Sciences; Fusion Energy Sciences; High Energy Physics; Nuclear Physics; and Isotope R&D and Production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed research topics must fall within the programmatic priorities of the chosen Office of Science program office as provided in the program announcement; applicants should select the single, most appropriate program office and align their proposal to its stated priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process — mandatory pre-application and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-applications are mandatory and are due on March 24, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET. Applications will be due on June 2, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting a pre-application by the stated deadline is required; missing the pre-application will preclude submission of a full application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full application eligibility — pre-application encouragement required
rubrics_metrics.description: Only those applicants whose pre-application is encouraged by DOE may submit full applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pre-application is a gating step: applicants should treat the pre-application as the primary competitive filter and ensure it clearly demonstrates fit and merit to receive encouragement to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process — competitive peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding will be competitively awarded on the basis of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals will be evaluated by peer review panels; applicants should prepare proposals to address peer-review evaluation expectations (e.g., scientific merit, alignment with priorities, feasibility), even though detailed review criteria are in the program announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program objective — stimulate new research directions in mission-critical areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The program will provide five-year awards to exceptional early career researchers ... to stimulate new research directions in mission critical areas supported by DOE’s Office of Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should emphasize novel concepts, new research directions, and relevance to mission-critical DOE science and energy objectives; framing impact and novelty is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned funding amount and appropriations caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Total planned funding is up to $145 million, with $79 million in Fiscal Year 2026 dollars and outyear funding contingent on congressional appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that total program funding and outyear support depend on congressional appropriations, which may affect award availability or number in future years.
